questions.q: Which cabins on the Carnatic were empty when she sailed?
choices: The captain's quarters
The two state-rooms Fogg had engaged
All of the second-class cabins below
The cabins booked by Fix for himself
questions.evidence: those which had been engaged by Phileas Fogg

questions.q: How did Passepartout end up on board the Carnatic?
choices: Fix carried him on board and left him in a cabin
He staggered to the quay and fell on deck
The police found him and put him on the ship by mistake
Fogg sent two sailors to bring him back from the tavern
questions.evidence: fell unconscious on the deck, just as the Carnatic was moving off

questions.q: What do the words "pursued even in his dreams by a fixed idea" suggest about Passepartout?
choices: He kept dreaming about the money Fix had offered him
Even asleep, he could not forget his duty to reach the Carnatic
He was having nightmares about the storm at sea
He kept thinking about Aouda and the night of her rescue at the pagoda
questions.evidence: The thought of a duty unfulfilled shook off his torpor

questions.q: What did Passepartout think about Fix's claim that Fogg had robbed the bank?
choices: He thought it might be true and was afraid
He thought it was nonsense
He thought Aouda must know the truth
He decided to ask his master about it
questions.evidence: Mr. Fogg is no more a robber than I am a murderer.

questions.q: What did Passepartout think of doing about Fix's secret?
choices: Telegraphing the gentlemen of the Reform Club about it from Yokohama at once
Waiting until London to tell Fogg, and having a good laugh about it
Telling the captain so that Fix would be put off the ship
Writing it all down in a letter to Aouda
questions.evidence: have a good laugh over it

questions.q: How did Passepartout learn that his master was not on the ship?
choices: A sailor told him Fogg had stayed in Hong Kong
His name was not on the passenger list
He searched every cabin on the ship one by one
He found a note from Fogg in his own cabin
questions.evidence: his master's name was not upon it

questions.q: "He fell thunderstruck on a seat." What does "thunderstruck" mean here?
choices: Very shocked
Hurt by lightning
Very sleepy
Wet with rain
questions.evidence: He fell thunderstruck on a seat.

questions.q: Whom did Passepartout blame most for his master missing the steamer?
choices: Himself alone, for drinking too much port
The captain of the Carnatic, for leaving early
Fix, who got him drunk to separate him from his master
The clerk at the steamer office, who gave wrong times
questions.evidence: it was still more the fault of the traitor

questions.q: What was Passepartout's money situation on the way to Japan?
choices: He had a few pounds left from shopping in Hong Kong
He had not a single penny, though his passage was paid
He had Fogg's carpet-bag full of banknotes with him
He had borrowed some money from a friendly sailor on the ship
questions.evidence: he had not a solitary shilling, not so much as a penny

questions.q: How did Passepartout behave at meals on the Carnatic?
choices: He was too upset to eat anything at all
He ate for Mr. Fogg, Aouda, and himself
He saved half of his food to sell in Japan
He only drank tea and ate a little rice
questions.evidence: ate for Mr. Fogg, Aouda, and himself

questions.q: Why didn't Passepartout go to the consuls for help right away?
choices: He didn't know where their offices were
He did not want to tell the story connected with his master
He was afraid the consuls would arrest him
He thought their offices would already be closed for the night
questions.evidence: he shrank from telling the story of his adventures

questions.q: What did Passepartout find in the smoking-houses of Yokohama?
choices: Fine stringy tobacco, not opium
Opium, just like in Hong Kong
Nothing, they were all closed
Sailors from the Carnatic
questions.evidence: not opium, which is almost unknown in Japan

questions.q: Why were the violets Passepartout found no good for supper?
choices: They had no smell
They were poisonous
They were too small
Birds had eaten them
questions.evidence: he found that they were odourless

questions.q: Why did Passepartout have to wait until morning for a meal?
choices: He had no money, and meat was scarce in Yokohama
The shops in Yokohama closed at noon every day
He had promised the purser to come back to the ship
He did not like the taste of rice or fish
questions.evidence: to postpone the meal he craved till the following morning

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Passepartout finding himself alone and penniless on the Carnatic and in Yokohama
Fogg and Aouda arriving in Yokohama and searching the town for Passepartout
Fix and Passepartout fighting on the deck of the Carnatic
Passepartout getting a job with the French consul in Japan
